source.title: Think in Safety: Unveiling and Mitigating Safety Alignment Collapse in Multimodal Large Reasoning Model
source.authors: Xinyue Lou; You Li; Ji-Nan Xu; Xiang-Yu Shi; Chi Chen; Kai-Yu Huang

record.tranche_reason: Tests a safety-oriented reasoning fine-tuning approach with behavioral safety benchmarks, conceptually bearing on whether safety reasoning can improve safety. It does not test the original first-token KL measurement or the specified bypass interventions.
record.gate_note: The study tests supervised fine-tuning with safety-oriented thought-process data (TiS) and reports safety outcomes. It does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples or ordinary benign instruction data, token-position KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, or localization to a small set of parameters. Its aggregate finding of higher jailbreak ASR in reasoning models concerns safety degradation associated with reasoning, not the specific fine-tuning or token-position claims.
record.test_reason: Table 1 compares 9 multimodal reasoning models with the safety-trained base models they were fine-tuned from. Reasoning training uses ordinary benign data (SFT or RL on reasoning tasks). Jailbreak ASR rises for most pairs, averaging about 10.57%. This bears on V2 in a new setting: multimodal reasoning fine-tuning. The TiS experiments are the authors' own mitigation method compared against Direct and other safety datasets. They measure no token-position depth and no robustness to prefilling, suffixes or decoding changes, so they do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that most MLRMs degrade in safety relative to their base models on jailbreak benchmarks, and degrade less, or sometimes improve, on safety-awareness benchmarks. Their TiS dataset with a safety-oriented thought process improves safety on both benchmark types and outperforms the other safety datasets. They also note that the thought process itself often contains harmful content.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA supervised fine-tuning of two multimodal reasoning models on a purpose-built safety dataset with explicit safety-oriented thought processes, rather than harmful-example fine-tuning or first-token interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Effect of retaining the thought component differs by benchmark: the authors report MM-SafetyBench as an exception; on that benchmark answer-only data has lower ASR than TiS with thought for both models.

fits_no_version.finding: Over 50% of thought processes are unsafe for four MLRMs on FigStep. Safe thoughts sometimes lead to unsafe answers, e.g. 46.60% for QVQ-Preview.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning models' intermediate chains of thought carry harmful content that is not consistent with final-answer safety.

fits_no_version.finding: TiS (safety SFT with reasoning) cuts jailbreak ASR below that of the VLGuard, MIS and SPA-VL baselines, and mostly beats answer-only data. The exception is MM-SafetyBench.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety fine-tuning data that includes explicit safety reasoning improves safety of reasoning models more than answer-only refusal data.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors note that evaluations rely substantially on model judges, which may misjudge subtle unsafe content, and that only representative MLRMs were evaluated. MSSBench safe and unsafe evaluation used a single sampled instruction per scenario; the paper also reports using human evaluation for MSSBench because of shortcomings in the safe-category setup.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted due to the row limit. Individual model results in Table 1, modality ablation results in Table 2, and other benchmark-specific thought/answer breakdowns were not catalogued as V7 results because they do not test the token-position or training-depth claim.

untested.parts: Only off-the-shelf reasoning models are compared with their bases. The study runs no controlled fine-tuning with known benign data or sample counts, and no text-only LLMs.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
The jailbreak benchmarks are typographic and visual prompt attacks. No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes are tested.
The authors do not examine why safety is shallow.
No training aimed at spreading safety beyond the first tokens, and no depth or prefill robustness measured.

missing.what: Per-model ASR and safety-score changes for each reasoning model vs its base model on all five benchmarks
Modality ablation: caption replacement of images changes ASR, mostly lowering it except for Llama-series models

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 linkage is rejected. TiS is a general safety-reasoning SFT mitigation with no token-depth measure, so its rows are method-performance results. The study's real bearing on the claim is the base vs reasoning-model comparison (V2). That comparison is uncontrolled: training recipes differ across third-party models (SFT and RL), and the evaluation relies on GPT-4o-mini and Llama Guard judges. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or test of whether a few to a few hundred such examples remove refusal.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data to test harmful compliance.
No per-token KL measurement or comparison of aligned and base models across response positions.
Jailbreak benchmarks are evaluated, but the study does not test compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes as mechanisms for bypass.
No weight or rank localization of safety behavior.
No test of whether the training data or objective causes first-token shallowness.

Tests safety-oriented thought-process fine-tuning and safety outcomes, but not token-position spread, whether safety is specifically deeper than the first response tokens, or robustness to prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes.

rows.subject: MLRMs (aggregate over models with corresponding foundation models)
rows.operation_detail: Compared jailbreak benchmark ASR with corresponding foundation models

conditions.value: reasoning model versus corresponding foundation model

rows.baseline: corresponding foundation models; exact aggregate baseline not stated
rows.note: The authors report this aggregate across reasoning models; the individual model results are in Table 1.
rows.check: Should be linked to V2. Benign reasoning fine-tuning of safety-trained base models raised jailbreak ASR by about 10.57% on average. The baseline is the base models in Table 1; the per-model pairs are not rowed.

rows.subject: R1-Onevision, LLaVA-CoT, Kimi-VL-Thinking, and Skywork-R1V (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated safety of generated thought processes
rows.value: exceeds 50 percent for each of the four models
rows.note: The text explicitly states that unsafe thought-process proportions exceed 50 percent for all four models; exact values are not stated in the text.

relationships.condition: Jailbreak benchmarks (FigStep, MM-SafetyBench, JailBreaKV) for most reasoning model vs base pairs: LLaVA-CoT, Mulberry-Llama, LlamaV-o1, R1-Onevision, Mixed-R1, SophiaVL-R1, Kimi-VL-Thinking, LMM-R1
relationships.reason: r37 gives an average ASR rise of about 10.57%. Per Table 1 (not rowed), LLaVA-CoT rose +29.00, +33.81 and +27.86, and R1-Onevision +5.00, +13.08 and +19.64.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose by about 10.57% on average, with LLaVA-CoT up 29.00, 33.81 and 27.86 and R1-Onevision up 5.00, 13.08 and 19.64.

relationships.condition: MM-Eureka vs InternVL-2.5-8B, and safety-awareness benchmarks (SIUO, MSSBench)
relationships.reason: From the text, since Table 1 is not rowed (see r37). MM-Eureka changes +0.80, +0.48 and -3.21 on the jailbreak benchmarks, essentially none. On SIUO, Kimi-VL-Thinking (+10.93), Mixed-R1 (+10.18) and SophiaVL-R1 (+11.38) improve. Erosion therefore depends on model and benchmark type.
relationships.display_finding: MM-Eureka changed by +0.80, +0.48 and −3.21 on the jailbreak benchmarks, essentially none, while Kimi-VL-Thinking (+10.93), Mixed-R1 (+10.18) and SophiaVL-R1 (+11.38) improved on SIUO.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TiS fine-tuning on R1-Onevision and LLaVA-CoT across FigStep, JailBreaKV, SIUO, and MSSBench
reader_labels.reason: TiS improves the reported safety outcomes relative to Direct on these benchmarks, and thought/answer category results also improve; see r1, r3-r5, r11, r13-r15, r21-r26, r28-r36.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MM-SafetyBench comparison of TiS with and without thought
reader_labels.reason: The answer-only ablation has lower ASR than TiS with thought on MM-SafetyBench for both models, an exception to the stronger results generally reported for retaining thought; see r2, r7, r12, r17.
